questions.question: Why can a JavaScript Map implement an LRU cache with O(1) operations?
options: It iterates in insertion order, so delete-and-reinsert refreshes a key and keys().next() gives the oldest
It has a built-in capacity limit
questions.explanation: Insertion-order iteration lets the first key act as the least recently used; re-inserting on access moves a key to the newest end.

questions.question: In the doubly linked list LRU, why does each node store its key?
options: So the evicted tail node's entry can be deleted from the hash map
questions.explanation: Eviction starts from the list's tail; without the key in the node, you cannot tell which map entry to remove.

questions.question: Why is the monotonic-stack solution to next greater element O(n) despite its nested while loop?
options: The while loop runs at most once per iteration
It is actually O(n log n)
Each index is pushed once and popped at most once
questions.explanation: Total pushes and pops are each at most n, so the amortised work across the whole pass is linear.

questions.question: A token bucket has capacity 3 and refills 1 token per second. Five requests arrive at t = 0, then three at t = 2 s. How many of the later three are allowed?
questions.explanation: The first three requests at t = 0 use all the tokens. By t = 2 s two tokens have refilled, so two of the later three pass.
